Challenge C088-CH2: Membranes in dairy plants foul quickly and need cleaning every week.
Detail: At two dairy plants we service — one near Temerin, one outside

content.text: {"expertise":[{"text":"Membrane bioreactors can be operated continuously with enzyme recycling through ultrafiltration to maintain high enzymatic activity while managing membrane fouling through backwash protocols.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-03519","field":"abstract","quote":"Enzyme retention was 87–92% across 14 days of continuous operation"}]},{"text":"Substrate accessibility and cellulose digestibility can be characterised using Simons' staining technique to quantify the effect of pre-treatment conditions on enzymatic degradation rates.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-03510","field":"abstract","quote":"Cellulose accessibility was characterised by the Simons' staining technique"}]},{"text":"Alkaline cleaning protocols for ultrafiltration membranes must balance flux recovery against membrane material degradation, with ceramic membranes showing superior fouling resistance compared to polymeric alternatives.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-03378","field":"abstract","quote":"Ceramic membranes showed consistently higher PWFR across all protocols"}]}],"fit":"partial","fitReason":"The researcher has direct experience with membrane fouling characterisation and enzymatic saccharification kinetics [SYN-PUB-03519, SYN-PUB-03510], but the publications focus on lignocellulosic biomass processing rather than dairy fat and protein fouling mechanisms specific to this challenge."}
